prompt.context: Our client, GGC Health, operates eight Ambulatory Surgical Centers (ASC) on the east coast. GGC Health has consistently been a profitable organization, but over the past two years, their ASCs' cumulative revenues have been flat at $400 million/year. The CEO of GGC Health is concerned about this and has hired your firm to increase revenues by 15%.
prompt.question: How would you help GGC Health increase its revenues by 15%?

clarifying_info.a: ASCs are modern health care facilities focused on providing same-day surgical care, including diagnostic and preventive procedures. They are seen as a more convenient alternative to hospital-based outpatient procedures.

clarifying_info.q: Who decides where surgery is performed?
clarifying_info.a: Physicians generally dictate where the surgery is performed. They can perform surgeries at hospitals or ASCs.
No, pricing increases are not possible.

clarifying_info.q: What is the revenue model for an ASC?
clarifying_info.a: ASC revenue is equal to the number of procedures performed in the facility multiplied by the expected reimbursement per procedure.

exhibits.title: Physician Group Membership by City
exhibits.shows: A stacked bar chart showing the percentage breakdown of physician specialties (Orthopedic, Neurology, Gastroenterology) in three cities: Charlotte, Indianapolis, and Nashville

exhibits.title: Average Reimbursement Rates Per Patient by Specialty
exhibits.shows: A table listing physician specialties and their corresponding reimbursement rate per patient

framework: Increase revenue at existing 8 ASCs: grow number of patients per doctor, number of doctors per facility, procedure volume/types, and prioritize high-reimbursement patients/surgeries

Expand revenue by opening new ASCs: analyze target markets, physician group partnerships, patient demographics, competitive landscape (existing ASCs, hospital strength), and regulatory/reimbursement environment

questions.prompt: GGC Health has researched three potential expansion cities: Charlotte (30 doctors), Indianapolis (25 doctors), and Nashville (16 doctors). Given management can open only one new ASC immediately, which city should GGC Health enter?
questions.guidance: Candidate should request Exhibit 1 (specialty breakdown by city), build a 3x3 matrix of doctors per specialty per city by multiplying total doctors by specialty %. An excellent candidate quickly eliminates Nashville because Indianapolis dominates it on every specialty (10 vs 8 ortho, 10 vs 4 neuro, 5 vs 4 gastro). The decision then becomes Charlotte vs Indianapolis, requiring revenue calculation in Q2.

math.setup: Multiply # of doctors in each city by specialty % from Exhibit 1 to get doctors per specialty per city
steps: Nashville eliminated: Indianapolis beats Nashville on every specialty (10>8, 10>4, 5>4)
math.answer: Eliminate Nashville immediately. Remaining comparison: Charlotte vs Indianapolis.

questions.prompt: Given patients per doctor per month are: Orthopedic=15, Neurology=10, Gastroenterology=12, calculate revenue per city and recommend which city to enter.
questions.guidance: Candidate needs to ask for reimbursement rates (Exhibit 2), then calculate revenue per doctor per year per specialty, multiply by number of doctors per specialty per city, and sum for total city revenue. Candidate should identify Indianapolis ($49.8M) as more attractive than Charlotte ($37.1M), but recognize that $49.8M alone falls short of the $60M target (15% of $400M).

math.setup: Revenue per doctor per year = (patients/month * 12) * reimbursement rate. Then multiply by # of doctors per specialty per city and sum.
steps: Indianapolis ($49.8M) is highest but still $10.2M short of $60M target
math.answer: Indianapolis is the best expansion city at $49.8M projected revenue, but opening one ASC alone does not meet the 15% ($60M) target. Additional same-site revenue initiatives are needed.

questions.prompt: Indianapolis alone does not achieve the $60M revenue target. Brainstorm how GGC Health could increase revenues at its current 8 ASC locations.
questions.guidance: Candidate should be structured, organized, and ideally group ideas into buckets. See brainstorming section for expected categories and ideas.

questions.prompt: GGC Health's current ASC sites do not offer urology, but the team believes 2 urology doctors can be added to all 8 current sites. Each urology doctor brings in 8 patients per month. Calculate the additional revenue from adding urology to all current ASCs.
questions.guidance: Candidate should use the urology reimbursement rate from Exhibit 2 ($8,000/patient). Total urologists = 8 sites * 2 = 16. Total patients/year = 16 * (8*12) = 1,536, rounded to 1,500. Revenue = 1,500 * $8,000 = $12M. This plus Indianapolis ($49.8M) = $61.8M, exceeding the $60M target.

math.setup: Total urologists across all sites * annual patients per urologist * reimbursement rate per patient
steps: Annual patients: 16 * (8 patients/month * 12 months) = 1,536 patients → round to 1,500
math.answer: $12M in incremental urology revenue. Combined with Indianapolis ($49.8M), total new revenue = $61.8M, meeting the 15% growth target.

brainstorming.prompt: How could GGC Health increase revenues at its current 8 ASC locations?

categories.name: Increase patients per doctor
ideas: Make ASC the preferred location for doctors by offering more control over environment
Improve scheduling efficiency and patient outcomes at ASCs
Provide doctors with a higher profit share for hitting volume targets

categories.name: Increase number of doctors per ASC
ideas: Recruit physicians for new procedure types (e.g., urology)
Improved physician outreach through sales and marketing efforts
Attract physicians from hospitals through better terms

categories.name: Optimize product/procedure mix
ideas: Prioritize high-reimbursement surgeries (e.g., neurology at $25K vs. orthopedic at $5K)
Expand into specialties not currently offered

categories.name: Optimize patient mix
ideas: Evaluate whether to accept Medicaid/Medicare patients vs. those with higher reimbursement
Increase proportion of patients with higher-reimbursement insurance plans

recommendation: Open a new ASC in Indianapolis, projected to generate $49.8M in new annual revenue
Add 2 urology doctors to each of the 8 existing ASC sites, generating an additional $12M in annual revenue
Combined, these two initiatives generate $61.8M in new revenue, exceeding the 15% ($60M) target
risks: No costs were considered in adding a new facility or procedure — cost/benefit analysis is needed
Indianapolis is not on the east coast and may be unfamiliar territory for management
Existing ASC capacity may not accommodate new surgeries
GGC Health may not be able to capture the expected physician/patient market share
Physicians may not bring in the expected number of patients
next_steps: Conduct a full cost/benefit analysis for the Indianapolis location
If still financially attractive, begin construction on the new Indianapolis ASC
Add urology surgeries to current 8 ASCs as soon as possible
Evaluate adding other new surgery types to existing sites
Consider expanding into more than one new location in future phases
